args.root_cause: `is_eligible` and `apply_discount` in library/discounts.py track redemptions in a module-level global set `_used_codes`. `apply_discount` adds `discount.code` to that set on every successful application, and `is_eligible` returns False for any code already in the set. Since the set is process-global and never cleared (and nothing is per-order), a multi-use code like SAVE10 applies once per process lifetime: the first order succeeds, every later order silently gets no discount, and a service restart resets the set (explaining the "works again for one more order" symptom only loosely, as the first order after restart then consumes it). The discount's `Discount` object itself is not deactivated; the state is purely this global set. The intended behavior (per the test named test_discount_object_is_reusable_across_separate_orders) is that discounts are not "used up" across orders.

Note: `test_discounts_stack_in_order` and `test_fixed_discount_does_not_go_negative` also share codes across tests (SAVE10, FLAT5), so they fail for the same reason.

args.summary: Root cause: library/discounts.py kept a process-global `_used_codes` set. apply_discount added each code to it and is_eligible rejected any code already in the set, so a multi-use code like SAVE10 only worked once per process lifetime. I removed the global set, its check in is_eligible, and its add in apply_discount, so eligibility now depends only on the subtotal vs. min_subtotal. This also fixes the cross-test leakage that made test_fixed_discount_does_not_go_negative and test_discounts_stack_in_order fail. Full suite: 29 passed.
